subs.name: 二氧化硅（石英砂）
subs.note: 原料，来源是沙子与石英。
subs.noteEn: The feedstock, from sand and quartz.

subs.name: 焦炭
subs.note: 还原剂，自己被氧化成 CO。
subs.noteEn: Reducer; itself oxidized to CO.

subs.name: 硅（粗硅 → 高纯硅）
subs.note: 第一步只得 98~99% 粗硅，第三步才沉积出高纯硅。
subs.noteEn: Step one gives only 98–99% crude; step three deposits pure Si.

subs.name: 一氧化碳
subs.note: 电弧炉尾气，可燃、有毒。
subs.noteEn: Toxic, flammable off-gas of the furnace.

subs.name: 氯化氢
subs.note: 第二步消耗、第三步再生，可循环利用。
subs.noteEn: Used in step two, regenerated in step three; recycled.

subs.name: 三氯氢硅
subs.note: 液态中间体，蒸馏即可除去硼、磷等杂质。
subs.noteEn: Liquid intermediate; distillation strips boron and phosphorus.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 还原剂，把硅从 SiHCl₃ 里重新放出来。
subs.noteEn: Reducer that frees silicon again from SiHCl₃.

term: 粗硅提纯与半导体级硅
oneLiner: 石英砂用焦炭还原得粗硅，转成三氯氢硅蒸馏后再氢还原，区熔得 9N 高纯硅。
oneLinerEn: Coke reduces quartz to crude Si; convert it to SiHCl₃, distill, reduce with H₂, then zone-refine to 9N.
detail: 三步提纯：石英砂与焦炭在电弧炉约 2000 ℃ 还原得冶金级粗硅；粗硅与 HCl 在铜催化下生成液态的三氯氢硅，蒸馏除去硼、磷等杂质；再用氢气在高温下还原，硅沉积在硅芯上，经区熔或直拉法制成单晶硅锭，纯度可达 99.9999999%（9N）。芯片用硅要求极高，因为痕量的硼、磷就会显著改变导电性——这也是废旧芯片值得回收提金的前提。
detailEn: Three steps: quartz sand plus coke in an arc furnace near 2000 °C gives metallurgical-grade silicon; it reacts with HCl over a copper catalyst to form liquid trichlorosilane, which is distilled to strip boron and phosphorus; hydrogen then reduces it back to silicon deposited on seeds, and zone refining or the Czochralski pull yields an ingot up to 99.9999999% (9N). Chip-grade silicon must be that pure because traces of boron or phosphorus already shift conductivity — which is exactly why scrap chips are worth reprocessing.

subs.name: 硫铁矿（黄铁矿）
subs.note: 廉价硫源，在沸腾炉中焙烧。
subs.noteEn: Cheap sulfur source, roasted in a fluidized bed.

subs.name: 氧气（空气）
subs.note: 两步都要用空气提供。
subs.noteEn: Supplied as air in two of the steps.

subs.name: 氧化铁（炉渣）
subs.note: 炉渣可返作炼铁原料或制水泥。
subs.noteEn: Slag goes back to ironmaking or cement.

subs.name: 二氧化硫
subs.note: 中间产物，也是酸雨主因，尾气须回收。
subs.noteEn: Intermediate; also the acid-rain gas, so off-gas is scrubbed.

subs.name: 三氧化硫
subs.note: 催化氧化的产物，不能直接用水吸收。
subs.noteEn: From catalytic oxidation; must not be absorbed by water directly.

subs.name: 五氧化二钒（催化剂）
subs.note: 加快平衡到达，不改变平衡位置。
subs.noteEn: Speeds up reaching equilibrium; shifts nothing.

subs.name: 发烟硫酸
subs.note: SO₃ 溶于 98.3% 浓硫酸的产物。
subs.noteEn: SO₃ dissolved in 98.3% sulfuric acid.

subs.name: 硫酸
subs.note: 既是吸收剂又是最终产品，稀释后出厂。
subs.noteEn: Both absorbent and final product, diluted before shipping.

oneLiner: 焙烧得 SO₂，V₂O₅ 催化氧化成 SO₃，再用 98.3% 浓硫酸吸收后稀释。
oneLinerEn: Roast to SO₂, oxidize over V₂O₅ to SO₃, absorb in 98.3% acid, then dilute.
detail: 三步：焙烧、催化氧化、吸收。SO₂ 氧化为 SO₃ 时气体分子数减小且放热，理论上低温加压有利，但低温下 V₂O₅ 活性不足，所以取 400~500 ℃、常压这个折中点。SO₃ 不直接溶于水，否则形成雾状硫酸难以沉降且腐蚀设备，工业用 98.3% 浓硫酸吸收。硫酸的产量长期被当作工业化的指标：化肥、石油精炼、冶金、蓄电池、洗涤剂全部依赖它。尾气中的 SO₂ 用氨法吸收制取硫酸铵，既省原料又防酸雨。
detailEn: Three stages: roasting, catalytic oxidation, absorption. Oxidizing SO₂ shrinks gas volume and gives off heat, so low temperature and high pressure favour it in theory — but V₂O₅ is inactive when cold, so plants compromise at 400–500 °C and near ambient pressure. SO₃ is never absorbed in water directly, which would make a mist of sulfuric acid that will not settle and eats the equipment; 98.3% acid does the absorbing. Sulfuric acid output has long been read as a proxy for industrialization: fertilizer, refining, metallurgy, batteries and detergents all depend on it. Off-gas SO₂ is scrubbed with ammonia to give ammonium sulfate, saving feedstock and preventing acid rain.

subs.name: 氨
subs.note: 由合成氨装置直接供料，两大工艺链相接。
subs.noteEn: Fed straight from the ammonia plant; two process chains meet.

subs.name: 氧气（过量空气）
subs.note: 氧化剂，吸收塔还要再通一次。
subs.noteEn: Oxidizer; passed in again in the absorber.

subs.name: 铂铑合金网（催化剂）
subs.note: 极贵且易中砷、铅中毒，需净制原料气。
subs.noteEn: Costly and easily poisoned by arsenic or lead; gas must be cleaned.

subs.name: 一氧化氮
subs.note: 无色，出装置即变红棕；水中吸收时又会逸出循环。
subs.noteEn: Colourless, browns on escape; recirculates from the water absorption.

subs.name: 二氧化氮
subs.note: 红棕色有毒气体，被水与氧吸收成酸。
subs.noteEn: Red-brown toxic gas, absorbed by water and oxygen into acid.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 吸收塔的液相，也是副产蒸汽的来源。
subs.noteEn: The absorber's liquid phase; also raises steam from the heat.

subs.name: 硝酸
subs.note: 产品，约 50~68%，可再浓缩。
subs.noteEn: Product, about 50–68%; can be concentrated further.

oneLiner: 氨在铂铑网上催化氧化成 NO，再氧化为 NO₂，在过量空气下用水吸收成硝酸。
oneLinerEn: Ammonia burns to NO over Pt-Rh gauze, oxidizes to NO₂, and is absorbed with excess air into nitric acid.
detail: 奥斯特瓦尔德法。氨氧化在约 800 ℃ 的铂铑网上瞬时完成且放热，反应热可维持自身温度，但必须防止砷、铅使催化剂中毒。NO 遇空气即变红棕色 NO₂；用水吸收时每 3 个 NO₂ 只有 2 个成酸、另 1 个回到 NO，所以工业上在吸收塔里大量通空气把 NO 反复氧化吸收，总结果相当于第四式。主要用途是硝酸铵与硝基化肥、炸药，以及尼龙的中间体己二酸；浓硝酸还用于金属钝化与蚀刻。尾气中的 NOx 用碱液或催化还原除去。
detailEn: The Ostwald process. Ammonia oxidation runs instantaneously on Pt-Rh gauze at about 800 °C and gives off enough heat to sustain itself, but arsenic and lead must be kept out or the catalyst dies. NO browns to NO₂ in air; water absorption turns only 2 of every 3 NO₂ into acid and sends 1 back to NO, so plants flood the absorber with air to re-oxidize and re-absorb it, which is what the fourth line summarizes. Uses: ammonium nitrate and nitrogen fertilizer, explosives, adipic acid for nylon; concentrated acid also passivates and etches metals. Tail-gas NOx is removed with alkali or catalytic reduction.

subs.name: 氧化铝（自铝土矿提纯）
subs.note: 原料，需先用氢氧化钠溶出重结晶（拜耳法）。
subs.noteEn: Feedstock, first dissolved in NaOH and recrystallized (Bayer process).

subs.name: 冰晶石（熔剂）
subs.note: 把电解温度从 2050 ℃ 降到约 960 ℃。
subs.noteEn: Drops the operating temperature from 2050 °C to about 960 °C.

subs.name: 碳素阳极
subs.note: 参与反应被消耗，需定期更换。
subs.noteEn: Consumed by the oxygen it meets; replaced regularly.

subs.name: 铝液
subs.note: 密度大于电解质，沉在槽底定期抽出。
subs.noteEn: Denser than the bath, so it pools at the bottom and is tapped.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 阳极产物，随即与碳块反应。
subs.noteEn: Anode product, which attacks the carbon immediately.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 阳极消耗的真实产物，也是碳排放主项。
subs.noteEn: The real anode output, and the plant's main emission.

oneLiner: 氧化铝溶进熔融冰晶石，在 960 ℃ 电解即可得铝，远低于直接熔化所需的 2050 ℃。
oneLinerEn: Alumina dissolved in molten cryolite electrolyzes at 960 °C — far below its 2050 °C melting point.
detail: 氧化铝熔点高达 2050 ℃，直接熔化电解既耗能又损毁内衬；溶入冰晶石 Na₃AlF₆ 后在 950~980 ℃ 就能通电分解，这是 Hall–Héroult 法的核心。阳极产生的氧会把碳块烧成 CO₂，所以阳极要不断补充，电耗与阳极材料占了成本大头——而回收一吨再生铝只需原铝约 5% 的能量。上游的拜耳法用浓 NaOH 溶出铝土矿中的 Al₂O₃，杂质作为红色赤泥排出，堆存是铝工业的主要环境负担。
detailEn: Alumina melts at 2050 °C, too hot to electrolyze directly without wrecking the lining; dissolved in cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) it breaks down at 950–980 °C, which is the core of the Hall–Héroult process. The oxygen liberated burns the carbon anode to CO₂, so anodes are eaten away and must be replaced — power and anodes dominate the cost, which is why recycling a tonne of aluminum takes only about 5% of the energy of primary metal. Upstream, the Bayer process leaches the ore with concentrated NaOH and discards the impurities as red mud, the industry's main waste burden.

subs.name: 粗铜（作阳极）
subs.note: 火法炼出的约 99%，含 Fe、Zn、Ni、Au、Ag 等杂质。
subs.noteEn: About 99% from smelting, holding Fe, Zn, Ni, Au and Ag.

subs.name: 铜离子（电解液）
subs.note: 阳极溶入、阴极析出，溶液浓度基本不变。
subs.noteEn: Enters at the anode, leaves at the cathode; strength stays steady.

subs.name: 电子（外电路）
subs.note: 阳极失电子溶解，阴极得电子析出。
subs.noteEn: Given up as the anode dissolves, taken up as copper plates out.

subs.name: 电解铜（阴极析出，99.95%+）
subs.note: 纯度达 99.95% 以上，导电用铜必须到这个级别。
subs.noteEn: 99.95%+; conducting copper has to reach this grade.

subs.name: 锌离子（进入溶液）
subs.note: 比铜活泼的杂质同溶但不析出，靠电位控制。
subs.noteEn: More active impurities dissolve but will not plate out at this potential.

subs.name: 阳极泥（金、银与铂族）
subs.note: 比铜惰性的金属不溶解，脱落沉入槽底。
subs.noteEn: Metals less active than copper never dissolve; they drop to the cell bottom.

term: 铜的电解精炼与阳极泥
termEn: Electrorefining Copper and the Anode Slime
oneLiner: 粗铜作阳极溶解、纯铜在阴极析出，不溶的金银铂族沉入槽底成为阳极泥。
oneLinerEn: The anode dissolves and pure copper plates out; insoluble Au, Ag and PGMs fall as anode slime.
detail: 火法炼出的铜约 99%，而导电用铜要求 99.95% 以上，靠电解精炼完成：粗铜作阳极、纯铜片作阴极、硫酸酸化的 CuSO₄ 溶液作电解液。通电后阳极上的铜溶解，在阴极按电位控制重新析出，比铜活泼的 Fe、Zn、Ni 虽一同进入溶液却不达析出电位，留在液里；比铜惰性的金、银和铂族金属根本不能溶解，只能从阳极脱落沉底，这就是阳极泥。它是冶炼厂提炼金银与铂族元素的主要原料，也是重要副产品收入。与电子废弃物提金相比，阳极泥里的金是火法富集的“顺带”产物，品位高且无需王水。
detailEn: Smelted copper is about 99% pure, but conducting copper needs 99.95%+, so it is electrorefined: blister copper as anode, a pure-copper sheet as cathode, acidified CuSO₄ solution as electrolyte. Copper dissolves off the anode and plates back under potential control; more active Fe, Zn and Ni enter the solution but never reach their deposition potential and stay there, while gold, silver and the platinum group cannot dissolve at all — they simply fall from the anode as slime. That slime is the chief feedstock for refining precious metals and a major by-product credit for the smelter. Unlike e-waste gold recovery, the gold in anode slime has already been concentrated by fire, at high grade and with no aqua regia involved.

subs.name: 重铬酸根（六价铬）
subs.note: 电镀、制革、颜料废水里的形态，氧化性强、致癌。
subs.noteEn: Form found in plating, tanning and pigment effluent; strong oxidizer, carcinogenic.

subs.name: 亚硫酸钠（还原剂）
subs.note: 酸性条件下把 Cr(VI) 还原为 Cr(III)，也可用硫酸亚铁。
subs.noteEn: Reduces Cr(VI) in acid; ferrous sulfate works as well.

subs.name: 氢离子（调 pH≈2~3）
subs.note: 酸性是还原反应的前提，常用硫酸调。
subs.noteEn: Acidity is required for the reduction; dosed with sulfuric acid.

subs.name: 铬离子（三价）
subs.note: 毒性远低于六价，且能形成难溶氢氧化物。
subs.noteEn: Far less toxic and readily precipitated as the hydroxide.

subs.name: 硫酸根
subs.note: 亚硫酸根被氧化的产物，留在水中。
subs.noteEn: What the sulfite becomes; remains dissolved.

subs.name: 氢氧根（加石灰）
subs.note: 调至 pH 8~9 使铬完全沉淀。
subs.noteEn: Raised to pH 8–9 to finish the precipitation.

subs.name: 氢氧化铬沉淀
subs.note: 压滤除去，滤饼属危险废物。
subs.noteEn: Filter-pressed out; the cake is hazardous waste.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 还原反应的产物，也作稀释介质。
subs.noteEn: Product of the reduction and the carrier of the whole process.

term: 含铬废水的还原沉淀处理
oneLiner: 酸性下用亚硫酸钠把六价铬还原为三价，再加石灰沉淀成 Cr(OH)₃ 滤除。
oneLinerEn: Reduce Cr(VI) to Cr(III) with sulfite in acid, then precipitate Cr(OH)₃ with lime and filter it out.
detail: 六价铬以 Cr₂O₇²⁻（酸性）或 CrO₄²⁻（碱性）存在，氧化性强、易穿透生物膜，是明确的致癌物；而三价铬溶解度低、毒性小得多。所以处理思路是“先还原、后沉淀”：酸性下投加亚硫酸钠或硫酸亚铁把 Cr(VI) 还原为 Cr³⁺，再加石灰调至弱碱性生成 Cr(OH)₃ 沉淀，压滤分离。滤饼属危险废物，不能随意填埋；清水需复检达标后排放。另一条路线是离子交换吸附或电解法回收，把铬回用于镀液，既省原料又减泥量。
detailEn: Chromium(VI) exists as Cr₂O₇²⁻ in acid and CrO₄²⁻ in alkali: a strong oxidizer that crosses cell membranes readily and a confirmed carcinogen, whereas Cr(III) is far less toxic and barely soluble. Hence the two-stage logic — reduce first, then precipitate: dose sulfite or ferrous sulfate in acid to bring Cr(VI) down to Cr³⁺, then add lime to make the solution mildly alkaline so Cr(OH)₃ falls out and can be filter-pressed. The cake is hazardous waste and cannot simply be landfilled; the clarified water is re-tested before discharge. The alternative route recovers chromium by ion exchange or electrolysis and returns it to the plating bath, saving both chemical and sludge.
